decoy: src/lib/astronomy/horizontal.ts (the failed patch went there because the bug report's named invariants live in that file's tests, but those invariants were already correct — the actual WGS84 symptom is in the satellite pipeline, not the celestial-body pipeline)
rationale: The WGS84 model only matters where the observer's position on Earth is dominant — that's the satellite look-angle path (look-angles.ts), where a 400 km LEO target amplifies any observer mislocation. The current observerEci treats the Earth as a sphere with RE=6378.137 km at every latitude, so geodetic inputs are interpreted as geocentric; at the poles this misplaces the observer by ~21 km (WGS84 polar radius is 6356.752 km), tilting close-satellite alt/az. horizontal.ts handles distant Solar-System bodies where the geodetic-to-geocentric offset is negligible (~0.95° topocentric parallax at the Moon) and the existing spherical treatment + parallax term is correct — its named invariants (vernal equinox → RA 0, ecliptic pole → Dec = 90-ε, meridian-at-lat zenith) all already hold. The prior fix commit a5cf0981f replaced RE with WGS84_A/WGS84_F/WGS84_E2 and the prime-vertical radius of curvature n in observerEci, confirming the true owner.
